legend: This is an interactive problem!

There's a hidden array a1,a2,…,aN%%ZSMJ0%% of N%%ZSMJ1%% distinct positive integers (where N%%ZSMJ2%% is odd); an incorrect copy of this array is stored in another hidden array b%%ZSMJ3%%. Each element of array b%%ZSMJ4%% is defined as follows:
b1=a2%%ZSMJ5%%
bN=aN−1%%ZSMJ6%%
bi=ai−1%%ZSMJ7%% or bi=ai+1%%ZSMJ8%% for each i%%ZSMJ9%% where 1<i<N%%ZSMJ10%% (one of the adjacent elements)

You need to determine whether there are two indices i%%ZSMJ11%% and j%%ZSMJ12%% (i≠j%%ZSMJ13%%, 1≤i,j≤N%%ZSMJ14%%) such that bi=bj%%ZSMJ15%%. If such indices exist, return them; otherwise, indicate that no such indices exist.
You can query the elements of arrays a%%ZSMJ16%% and b%%ZSMJ17%% using the following operations:
1 i: returns the value of ai (1≤ai≤109)%%ZSMJ18%%
2 i: returns the value of bi (1≤bi≤109)%%ZSMJ19%%
You can ask up to a maximum of 20%%ZSMJ20%% queries.
Interaction
First, you must read a line containing a single integer T%%ZSMJ21%% (1≤T≤100%%ZSMJ22%%) denoting the number of test cases. Then follows a description of the interaction for T%%ZSMJ23%% test cases.
For each test case, you must first read a line containing one integer N%%ZSMJ24%% (3≤N≤2 001, N is odd%%ZSMJ25%%).
Then interaction starts. You can print one line, containing:
1 x (Ask about ax%%ZSMJ26%%): Then, read one line, consisting of one integer, ax%%ZSMJ27%%.
2 x (Ask about bx%%ZSMJ28%%): Then, read one line, consisting of one integer, bx%%ZSMJ29%%.
3 i j (The answer: two indices i%%ZSMJ30%%, j%%ZSMJ31%%, where bi=bj%%ZSMJ32%% or -1 -1 if there are no such two indices): Then, proceed to the next test if there is any; otherwise, terminate.
After outputting each line, don't forget to flush the output. For example:
fflush(stdout) in C/C++;
System.out.flush() in Java;
sys.stdout.flush() in Python;
flush(output) in Pascal;
See the documentation for other languages.
